messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: 5xx spike on LumenCorp VPC gateway (us-east-1) — websocket disconnects + client retries. Alert group: gateway-streaming-errors > 5% for 10m

maria (oncall): acked. I'm on it. grabbing logs and will triage.

customer-ops (LumenCorp): seeing thousands of reconnects from our app gateway starting ~09:10 UTC. Users report partial responses / truncated streams.

ajay (eng-runtime): can you paste the gateway logs (headers + upstream status) or give example request ids? we want to know if it's 504s or socket-level resets.

customer-ops (LumenCorp): example request id: "req-4b8f9a" — gateway shows repeated 502 from the backend and client retry loops.

ryan (sre): quick summary from infra metrics: dedicated pool for LumenCorp (pool-lumen-1) cpu at 92%, gRPC worker queue depth spiking, KV-cache hit rate dropped from 78% -> 12% at incident start. suggests cache churn on long-tail prompts.

maria (oncall): initial mitigation idea: temporarily increase proxy read timeout and disable automatic client retries at the API gateway to prevent retry storms. paging ops to prod-network.

tasha (support): CC'ing Lumen eng contact (on their side) to coordinate a graceful client backoff. They confirmed they auto-retry on 5xx up to 3 times with no jitter.

ajay (eng-runtime): logs from model-host show many pending KV-restore ops per connection. suspect a serialization/blocking path in the quantized runner under heavy cache miss. Also seeing repeated websocket closure error: "EOF" paired with "write: broken pipe".

maria (oncall): actions I'm taking now:
- set a scoped per-tenant connection cap on the public LB to 300 (was unlimited)
- raise backend proxy read_timeout from 30s -> 60s for lumen routes
- pushed temporary NGINX config to drop naive client retries header `x-retry` (so our infra won't attempt to replay)

ajay (eng-runtime): good. additional option: route Lumen traffic to fallback model variant that is lower mem footprint (lumen-variant-quant-8bit) to reduce KV pressure. can do a canary shift 10% -> 50% if stable.

ryan (sre): paging cloud-net on increasing burst capacity for pool-lumen-1 — requesting +1 GPU warm standby (best-effort) and increase kube pod priority for runtime pods servicing that pool.

incident-bot: -> oncall handoff scheduled in 35m to ajay (next shift)

maria (oncall): update from client: they disabled client-side aggressive retries and added exponential backoff. reconnects dropped ~40% but we still have high latencies for long streams.

ajay (eng-runtime): executed quick canary: shifted 10% of sessions to lumen-variant-quant-8bit at 09:34 UTC. Initial results: 90th p50 latency 18% lower, KV restore time per-conn down 40%. No errors yet from the canary cohort.

tasha (support): Lumen ops says some business-critical customers still see truncation. They want an ETA and request that we keep them in the loop every 15m.

maria (oncall): rolling to 40% now. also applied a per-tenant token-rate throttle to limit request concurrency for long-run streams. command snippet:
```
# apply tenant concurrency limit
rbacctl set-limit --tenant lumen --concurrency 300
```

ajay (eng-runtime): logs after 40% shift show backend queues draining, errors falling from 6.2% -> 1.1% over 12 minutes.

ryan (sre): cloud-net confirmed they can spin up the warm standby GPU, ETA ~18m. enabling it now as safety.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation progress: retries suppressed, variant canary, tenant throttles applied. Severity downgraded from SEV-2 -> SEV-3.

tasha (support): LumenOps: "we're seeing stable behavior for the majority of sessions, thanks. A small set of high-concurrency customers still impacted (banking flows)."

maria (oncall): next steps for stability:
- finish canary to 100% only if error rate stays <1.5% for 20m
- coordinate with infra to keep warm standby until end of day
- postmortem runbook note: trigger automatic fallback to low-mem variant when KV-hit < 20% for 5m

ajay (eng-runtime): agreed. I'm also going to open a short-term patch to make KV-restore async-safe to reduce head-of-line blocking — target PR in ~4hrs, hotfix timeline TBD.

customer-ops (LumenCorp): appreciate the quick work. small ask: can you provide a short incident summary we can share with our execs?

maria (oncall): will draft summary after we stabilize. for now: cause = retry storm + KV cache churn leading to backend saturation; mitigation = suppress retries, route to low-memory variant, throttle per-tenant concurrency, warm standby.

ryan (sre): moving to monitoring mode. will keep oncall rotation updated. handing off to ajay in 20m for runtime followup.

ajay (eng-runtime): taking over after 09:55 UTC. ping me for any dev/runtime escalation.

incident-bot: handoff: from maria (oncall) -> ajay (eng-runtime) at 09:55 UTC.

maria (oncall): wrapping up. recording incident channel notes and tagging for postmortem. :thumbsup:

customer-ops (LumenCorp): thanks team. we'll standby for the executive summary and timeline.

ajay (eng-runtime): note for postmortem: consider adding per-tenant adaptive fallback that automatically switches to quantized variant when latency thresholds exceeded for X minutes — avoids manual interventions.

maria (oncall): logged action items and assigned owners. closing live mitigation update; will reopen thread if errors creep back up.

incident-bot: thread closed (mitigation in place)"
